messages.author: 05954d53fb9c89d2
messages.subject: Unable to run the Bernoulli example in STATA STAN 2.14.0
parts:
Hi all,
I'm a beginner in STAN. 
I have STATA 14.0 MP, I was not able to run the Bernoulli example in the STAN help file. I tried all four methods in the example to combine the STAN model with my do file, all returned the same error message. Please see below my commands and the error message. I'm also attaching my STATA log file. Can someone help me to solve the issue?

Thank you very much
Best
Jing

Commands:
/* Version 4: specify the model inline, so it is written to the
 text file of your choosing but everything is controlled from the do-file
 (the Charles Opondo method) */

// make the data
set more off
clear all
set obs 10
gen y=0
replace y=1 in 2
replace y=1 in 10
count
global N=r(N)

global cmdstandir "U:\NON_PROJECT_DATA\Jing\cmdstan-2.14.0\examples\bernoulli"
// write the model from Stata into a plain text file
tempname writemodel
file open `writemodel' using "mystanmodel.stan", write replace
#delimit ;
foreach line in
        "data { "
        "  int<lower=0> N; "
        "  int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N];"
        "} "
        "parameters {"
        "  real<lower=0,upper=1> theta;"
        "} "
        "model {"
        "  theta ~ beta(1,1);"
        "  for (n in 1:N) "
        "    y[n] ~ bernoulli(theta);"
        "}"
{;
        #delimit cr
        file write `writemodel' "`line'" _n
}
file close `writemodel'

// call Stan
stan y, modelfile("mystanmodel.stan") cmd("$cmdstandir") globals("N") load mode


Error message:

file U:\NON_PROJECT_DATA\Jing\cmdstan-2.14.0\examples\bernoulli\output.csv not found

r(601);

I see a potential problem at line 13 where $cmdstandir is pointed not at the CmdStan directory but its Bernoulli example subdirectory. If you change that to:

global cmdstandir "C:\Users\jdong\Documents\cmdstan-2.14.0"
you might just be OK.
I suspect the missing file error messages indicate that CmdStan has not run at all and line 13 would do that. A quick way to test is to remove any "mystanmodel.*" files from both the working directory and the cmdstandir, then run it again. If my hunch is right, there will be mystanmodel.stan but not .hpp or .exe - because it couldn't find the CmdStan binaries.

Do let us know how it goes. If this is a different serious problem then I really want to know about it.

Robert
